success_patterns: Verbatim archive hits (J! Archive, GitHub jeopardy dumps) were copied exactly. This is already covered by Rule 3 (Bob Mackie, Pascal).

Definition-style clue ('It's the part of a racetrack from the last turn to the finish line'): dictionary passages repeat the definition word for word beside a headword in the page title. The agent answered with that headword (Homestretch) instead of paraphrasing the definition.
'Title character of this film' clue: the agent answered with the work's title (Il Postino), not the character's own name (Mario) or the poet named in the clue.
Referent-type matching worked ('this country' -> China, 'these birds' -> plural Owls, 'this character' -> Richard III with the regnal numeral). These are already covered by Rules 2 and 4.
Person-description clues (Johnny Cash) were answered with the full name that every passage ties to all the clue details. This is already covered.

patch.reasoning: Nearly every success came from rules already in the skill. Two patterns that recur across many batches are only implicit: (a) definition-style clues, where dictionary passages echo the clue and the headword in the page title is the answer, and (b) 'title character of this <work>', where the answer is the work's title. A short, targeted line for each reinforces them without the broad rewrites that earlier steps had rejected.

edits.target: Take the answer that follows the clue, even if the whole context is one short passage.
edits.content: - Definition-style clues ('It's the part of a racetrack from the last turn to the finish line') are answered by the defined WORD. Dictionary and glossary passages repeat the definition almost verbatim, and their titles or first words give the headword ('Homestretch - definition of homestretch ...'). Match the clue's wording to those definitions and answer with the headword exactly as it appears there, not a paraphrase or a longer description.

edits.target: 'One of these <role/title>' ('the 14th one of these spiritual leaders') asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content: - 'The title character of this film / play / book' (clue: 'Poet Pablo Neruda befriends the title character of this recent film set in Italy') asks for the WORK's title ('Il Postino'). Do not answer with the character's personal name or with the person already named in the clue. Drop quotation marks around the title.
